messages:
tim: Quick Q — starting POC with FinDrive. They prefer PrivateLink (interface endpoint) to our connector but have an on-prem Windows outbound proxy and want a private DNS stub for service discovery. Any immediate blockers or caveats?
kevin: We can support interface endpoints + private DNS, but a few caveats: PrivateLink means traffic lands on the endpoint ENI in their VPC (we NAT to our connector). If they need original client src IP for allowlisting, PrivateLink alone won't preserve it. Peering or adding a static EIP on our outbound connector are options. :mag:
raj: Netops checklist: for Interface Endpoint -> ensure endpoint SG allows inbound 443 from the consumer subnets. If connector talks back to on-prem proxy, they must allow outbound 443 to the proxy IP. Also, Windows VPN + proxy combos often run into MTU issues — recommend MSS clamp to 1400 for the POC.
kevin: Pricing note for the quote: PrivateLink has per-ENI and data-processing costs; VPC peering avoids interface charges but may be more ops-heavy across accounts. I'll include delta pricing (low/med/high throughput scenarios).
tim: They use certificate pinning for their client apps — does that affect TLS termination with PrivateLink?
raj: PrivateLink is L4 to the service endpoint. If our connector terminates TLS (typical for hosted connectors), certs presented to clients matter. If they pin our cert, we need to coordinate cert provisioning. If they require mTLS, we can configure mTLS on the connector but will need their client certs and KMS access details.
kevin: DNS stub options: we can create a Private Hosted Zone pointing at the interface endpoint DNS name, or they can use VPC DNS stub mapping. For Windows clients that cache DNS via GPO/WinDNS, remind their desktop team to push a flush or lower TTL during cutover.
raj: Firewall snippet for their net team (POC):
```
# FinDrive POC allowlist
Source: 198.51.100.45   # on-prem proxy IP
Dest: 10.12.34.56       # interface endpoint ENI (example)
Ports: 443/TCP
Notes: If choosing VPC peering instead, add route entry for 10.0.0.0/8 -> peering attachment.
```
kevin: Also flag: if TLS inspection is enabled on their proxy, cert pinning + inspection will break. Need clear stance: either disable TLS inspect for connector traffic or provide pinned certs to their proxy team.
deploy-bot: heads-up: POC connector deploy window scheduled Thu 09:00 UTC. Rollback window 10:30 UTC.
alex-cust: Thanks, this is great. Can you send a one-pager checklist and the pricing delta PrivateLink vs Peering? I'll queue the firewall ticket once I have the snippet.
kevin: Will prepare checklist + three-tier pricing (non-binding) by EOD. @raj can you confirm MTU 1400 and whether we should provide an EIP option to preserve src IP for their allowlist?
raj: Confirmed: MTU recommendation = 1400. We can offer an EIP on our outbound connector for source-IP preservation; will need to allocate and include in the network plan. I'll attach a short IPTables MSS clamp snippet if they need it.
tim: Awesome — thanks everyone :thumbsup:
